headline: US Congressional Ukraine Caucus warns of forced-deportation risk

sources: AP via LaPresse (Lubinets); RFE/RL via EuropeSays (Caucus statement; no violations first two days)

sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT] The six-day Oleshky ceasefire (in effect since Oct 27, until 22:59 Moscow time Nov 1) is holding with no violations in its first two days per Ukrainian and US officials via RFE/RL, and a humanitarian operation is working to deliver food/medicines to ~2,000 remaining residents and evacuate those who wish to leave (AP Oct 28, Lubinets). A US representative will join Russian/Ukrainian civilian officials on the ground once the road is demined and aid delivered. The bipartisan Congressional Ukraine Caucus (Kaptur, Quigley, Fitzpatrick, Wilson) welcomed the truce Oct 28 while warning of reports Russian authorities were preventing evacuation to Ukrainian-controlled territory; Lubinets says evacuees will be free to choose Ukraine or Russia. STILL NOT CONFIRMED: any convoy arrival, aid delivery completion, or evacuation numbers on mission-day Oct 29 itself.
sections.what_verified: 2 declared families: AP T1 (via LaPresse), RFE/RL T3 STATE (US-funded).
sections.what_disputed: No convoy/evacuation confirmation for Oct 29 retrieved; Ukrainian authorities asked media not to publish operation details (routes/timings), so absence of confirmation is not evidence of failure. Deportation-fear reports are allegations via the Caucus, not confirmed transfers.
sections.why_matters: Day 3 in Oleshky: the truce holds, aid is moving -- but the test is not the ceasefire, it is whether residents are free to choose Ukraine. Congress just warned about deportations.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE -- Oleshky day 3: truce holding, humanitarian operation under way (AP Oct 28); US Congressional Ukraine Caucus warns of forced-deportation risk (Oct 28, via RFE/RL)

totw_analysis: Our read: Day 3 in Oleshky: the truce holds, aid is moving -- but the test is not the ceasefire, it is whether residents are free to choose Ukraine. Congress just warned about deportations. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Humanitarian opening -- or a deportation trap? Free choice of destination is the test the Caucus named.
